why_not: I'd probably try the free tricks at Friday dinner, but I'm not typing my card into some website for an app that isn't even in the App Store. If it's not on the store, I don't know who's behind it or how to get my money back.

It's not in the App Store, so I can't find any reviews, and I have no idea who made it. I'm not putting my card into some website for an app I install from the browser. On top of that I'm not a magician, and I'd probably mess it up at Friday dinner in front of the whole family.

why_yes: I'm at a party almost every weekend and I already do phone tricks, so a word showing up in my own gallery or calculator is exactly what I'd show off. I'd try the free tricks first, and if one fools my husband I'd pay the 99 that same night.

I already pay for mentalism apps like this, and a Hebrew one I can use at Israeli birthdays and events is something I don't have. 99 shekels once is less than what I charge for ten minutes of a show, so if the free tricks hold up I'll buy it to compare with what I own.

I already own a few paid mind-reading apps, and 99 ₪ one time is nothing for me. A Hebrew version that puts the word in the Photos gallery, the calculator or a fake call fills a real gap in my kit, but I'd only pay after the free tricks fool my own family.

I already pay for magic stuff, and a phone mind-reading kit in Hebrew with gallery, notes, calculator and search reveals is the kind of thing I'd love to show my WhatsApp groups. If the free tricks actually fool my partner, I'd pay the 99 ₪ that same evening.

If the free tricks actually fool my friends at the next party, 99 shekels for lifetime is nothing to me, I'd pay that night just to have more tricks for the WhatsApp crowd. But I only pay after a free trick works, not before.
